html:
The Third Sacred War was fought from 356 to 346 BCE over control of the sanctuary of Apollo at Delphi, home of the oracle of Delphi. It drew in most of Greece and ended by giving Philip II of Macedon a central place in Greek affairs.

The council that ran Delphi, led at the time by Thebes, fined the small region of Phocis for farming land sacred to Apollo. Rather than pay, the Phocians seized Delphi itself. They then spent the temple's treasure, centuries of offerings, to hire large mercenary armies, and for a while beat everyone sent against them.

Philip entered the war in Thessaly. In 352 BCE he crushed the Phocians at the Battle of the Crocus Field. Athens blocked his way south at Thermopylae for some years, but in 346 BCE Athens made peace with him, and Phocis surrendered. Phocis lost its seats on the Delphic council and they went to Philip, who now presided over the Pythian Games. Demosthenes saw the outcome as a disaster. An earlier First Sacred War had also been fought over Delphi.
